title: Tensor-unit component of the scalar-first projection
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring, f : X → Y a morphism of schemes, L = Lf* and R = Rf* on derived categories of internal Λ-modules, and K a derived module on X. Form the scalar-first natural projection B ⊗ R(K) → R(L(B) ⊗ K) as the right-adjoint projection map of L ⊣ R with both tensor bifunctors flipped and the canonical generic derived tensor comparison, equal to the native oplax tensor comparison. Its component at the tensor unit B = 1 is an isomorphism.

source.place: Finite free coefficient extensions: the unit case before finite direct sums and cones

proof.text: For an arbitrary monoidal adjunction with tensor comparison δ and unit comparison η, transpose the projection followed by R(η tensor id) and R(leftUnitor) under the adjunction. Counit naturality and tensor interchange reduce the transposed equality to oplax left unitality. Thus this composite is the left unitor of R(K).

Identify the generic derived tensor comparison with the native comparison, then specialize to the native derived module-object adjunction and its oplax monoidal pullback. Its unit comparison is the native unit isomorphism. The two maps after the projection and the resulting left unitor are invertible, so cancellation proves that the unit component of the projection is invertible. The explicitly named equality of the oplax tensor field with the native comparison keeps the construction folded.

proof_origin.place: Finite free coefficient extensions, unit calculation; native oplax left-unitality and adjunction
